AgentInfo.description: One agent the model can call.

description.description: What it's for, in one line.

sessionId.description: An open session; its project's agents are listed.

AgentSource.description:
Where an agent's definition comes from. A project's overrides a
user's, which overrides a built-in one of the same name.

ApprovalDecision.description: Yes or no to a tool call.

oneOf.description: Run it, and the same command or file again this session.
Don't run it, and tell the model why.

ApprovalPolicy.description:
Who answers a session's approvals, questions and loop-cap decisions.
Codex's `approvalPolicy` names the same choice.

oneOf.description:
Nobody is there to ask, as in `koda exec`: Koda approves what the
mode allows, refuses destructive actions and anything outside the
sandbox, answers a question with nothing and goes on at the loop
cap. Each request is still sent, followed at once by
`serverRequest/resolved`, so a reader sees what was decided.

BackgroundTerminal.description: A background process that is still running.

osPid.description: The operating system's id for the process leading its group.

processId.description: Its id, for `terminate`: the process group's id, as a string.

startedAt.description: When it started, in Unix milliseconds. Koda's own; Codex has none.

BackgroundTerminalExit.description: A background process that exited by itself.

exitCode.description: Its exit code; absent when a signal ended it.

terminated.description:
How many were running and are now being stopped. Koda's own; Codex
answers with nothing.

BackgroundTerminalsExitedNotification.description:
`session/backgroundTerminals/exited`: background processes the model
started have exited by themselves, and the model is being told, as
Claude Code tells Claude when a background task finishes. Its
`turnId` is the turn that tells it: a running one, or one Koda starts
for it when the session is idle. A process a client or Koda stopped
isn't reported.

turnId.description: The turn that tells the model.

BackgroundTerminalsListResponse.description:
The answer to `session/backgroundTerminals/list`: the running ones,
oldest first.

waiting.description:
Whether the session will start a turn by itself for the model's
background commands: one is still running, or has ended and the
model hasn't been told yet. A sub-agent's commands don't count, nor
do processes an ordinary command left running.
Koda's own; `koda exec` waits while it's true, as `claude -p` waits
for background work.

BackgroundTerminalsTerminateParams.description:
`session/backgroundTerminals/terminate`: stop one, and whatever it
started.

terminated.description: Whether it was running and is now being stopped.

ClientInfo.description: A client's name and version, such as `koda-cli` `0.7.0`.

oneOf.description: A precondition stopped it; nothing changed.
The summary call failed; nothing changed.
Context passed the auto-compact threshold before a model call.
The provider rejected a request as too long.
The estimate was past the window, so history was dropped unsummarized.
The client asked for it with `session/compact/start`.

The turn's final reply left the context past the after-turn
threshold; it ran before `turn/completed`.

ConfigBatchWriteParams.description: `config/batchWrite`: change several keys at once, as Codex's does.

edits.description: The changes, applied in order; all or none.

expectedVersion.description:
Write only if the file is still at this version (from `config/read`
or an earlier write); otherwise refused with
[`ConfigWriteErrorCode::ConfigVersionConflict`].

ConfigEdit.description: One change: a key, its new value (`null` removes it) and how to merge.

mergeStrategy.description: How the value merges; for Koda's keys, both replace it.

value.description:
The value: a string, or for `mcp_servers.<name>` a server
([`crate::mcp::McpServerConfigValue`]); `null` removes the key.

ConfigLayer.description: A layer, its version and its values.

config.description: Every value it holds, Koda's keys or not.

version.description:
Its version, `sha256:` of its values; pass it as
`expectedVersion` to write only if nothing changed since.

ConfigLayerSource.description:
Where a value comes from: the user's file, or this run's `-c` values
over it. Codex also has managed and project layers.

oneOf.description:
`-c key=value` on the command line that started the host, for this
run only.

includeLayers.description: Also return each layer and its values.

ConfigReadResponse.description:
The answer to `config/read`: the settings, where each came from, and,
when asked, the layers. A key nothing sets is absent, and a new session
then uses the host's own.

origins.description:
The layer each value comes from, by dotted key path
(`model_providers.lm-studio.base_url`).

ConfigWarningNotification.description:
`configWarning`: something in a config file needs a look, such as a key
Koda doesn't know, which it loads past. In Codex's shape.

config.description: The settings as saved now, `-c` values included.

overriddenMetadata.description: With `okOverridden`: a `-c` value wins over what was written.

retry.description: The retry, when there is one.

turnId.description: The turn, when it happened in one.

willRetry.description: Whether Koda will try again. The turn goes on if so.

ErrorObject.description: What went wrong with a request.

code.description: One of the codes in [`codes`], or a Koda code.

data.description: Detail for a program, if any.

ErrorResponse.description: The answer to a request that failed.

id.description: The request's id; `null` when it couldn't be read.

ExecSummary.description: `exec/summary`: the run as a whole. Only `koda exec` sends it, last.

success.description: Whether the run succeeded. An interrupted turn is not a failure.

toolCalls.description: The agent's own tool calls, by tool.

turnStatus.description: How the turn ended; `None` if it never did.

usage.description:
Everything stored for the session, sub-agents and the earlier turns
of a resumed session included.

usageByAgent.description: `usage` by agent. The session's own calls are under `main`.

FeedbackSaveParams.description:
`feedback/save`: Codex's fields, less `extraLogFiles` and `tags`, which
nothing in Koda sends.

classification.description:
What kind of report: `bug`, `bad_result`, `good_result` or `other`,
Codex's names.

includeLogs.description:
Whether the ZIP holds the logs and session history, which can quote
prompts, commands and tool output. Without it, only the report.

reason.description: What happened, in the user's words.

savePath.description:
Where to write the ZIP on the host: an absolute path that doesn't
exist yet, as Codex requires.

sessionId.description: The session it's about, if any.
The session it's about, if any.

FileUpdateChange.description: A change to one file, in Codex's `FileUpdateChange` shape.

diff.description: For a change, the unified diff; for a new file, its content.

path.description: The file, as the tool call names it.

createdAt.description: When it was set, in Unix seconds.

timeUsedSeconds.description: Time its turns have taken, in seconds.

tokenBudget.description: The tokens it may use, if limited.

tokensUsed.description:
Tokens its turns have used: input not read from the cache, plus
output.

updatedAt.description: When it last changed, in Unix seconds.

oneOf.description:
Stopped because no progress could be made: the model said so, a turn
failed, or three turns in a row did nothing.
Its token budget is used up.
The model found the objective achieved.

GoalVerdict.description: What a goal's evaluator found after a turn.

oneOf.description: The goal holds; `session/goal/updated` follows with it complete.
Not yet; the next turn on the goal takes the reason as guidance.

It can never be satisfied; `session/goal/updated` follows with it
blocked.

ImageInput.description: An image sent with a turn's input.

InitializeParams.description: The client says who it is.

InitializeResponse.description: The server says what it is and which protocol it speaks.

oneOf.description:
What the user said: a turn's prompt, or steering text added while it
ran. Steering texts that reached the model together are one item.

clientMessageIds.description: The client's ids for the messages it carries, where it gave them.

mentions.description:
The files and directories it mentioned. The model was sent their
contents after the text; the item carries only the paths.

text.description: The text, as the user wrote it.

oneOf.description: Text from the model. Complete text on `item/completed`.

text.description: The text so far: empty when it starts.

oneOf.description: The model's reasoning, where the provider shows it.

text.description: The text so far: empty when it starts.

changes.description:
The file changes it would make, when Koda asked about it or
blocked it: Codex's `fileChange` item's `changes`, carried on
Koda's one tool-call item.

detail.description:
What the call would do, in a line, when Koda asked about it or
blocked it.

effect.description:
What it does, as Koda classifies the call, the effect an approval
names, so a client can colour or group it. Absent in turns stored
before Koda sent it.

id.description: The call's id, from the model.

output.description:
What the model reads: the tool's output, or why it didn't run.
Set on completion.

progress.description:
The notices sent about it as `item/toolCall/progress` while it
ran, in order: a sub-agent's, for an `InvokeAgent` call. Set on
completion. A skill's change of tool scope is sent once its call
has completed, so it isn't here.

oneOf.description: Context compaction: old history summarized or dropped to make room.

contextPercent.description: Context used when it began, in percent, where it was measured.

messagesRemoved.description: Rows taken out of the context, when completed.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed.

summaryTokens.description: Estimated size of the summary, when there is one.

completedAtMs.description: When it completed, in Unix milliseconds. Codex's `completedAtMs`.

parentItemId.description: On a sub-agent's items: the tool call that started the sub-agent.
On a sub-agent's items: the tool call that started the sub-agent.

startedAtMs.description: When it started, in Unix milliseconds. Codex's `startedAtMs`.

agent.description: The agent new sessions run: a built-in, or one from an agent file.

file_mentions.description:
Whether a mentioned file is sent with its contents (on when unset),
or only its path.

mcp_servers.description: The MCP servers every new session starts, by name.

mode.description: The mode a new session starts in.

model.description:
The model a new session starts with: an alias such as `claude-opus`,
which follows its line, or an id.

model_context_window.description:
The context window to assume, in tokens, for a server that doesn't
report its own.

model_input_modalities.description:
What the model takes besides text, `text`, `image` or `pdf`,
replacing Koda's table for it; unset for the table.

model_max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens a reply may use.

model_post_turn_compact_threshold_percen.description:
Context used, in percent, past which a turn compacts after its
final reply; 0 or none turns it off.

model_providers.description: Settings per provider, by provider id.

model_reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning effort a new session asks for.

model_thinking_budget.description: A thinking budget in tokens, for Gemini models.

review_model.description:
The model `/review` runs on, as Codex's `review_model`; the
session's own when unset.

sandbox.description: What sandboxed commands may do beyond Koda's defaults.

sessionId.description:
The session whose servers to list. Without one, the configured servers,
none of them started.

LoopCapDecision.description: Whether a turn at its cap goes on.

LoopCapParams.description:
`turn/loopCap/requestDecision`: the turn reached its iteration cap.
Until it is answered the turn waits.

oneOf.description: Told the model to change course; the turn goes on.
The model didn't, so the turn stops.

McpAuthStatus.description: How Koda authenticates to a server; Codex's values.

oneOf.description:
An HTTP server with neither a bearer token nor a sign-in: it may need
none, or answer 401.
A bearer token from an environment variable.

McpResource.description: One resource a server offers, MCP's `Resource`.

description.description: What it is, as the server says.

McpServerConfigValue.description:
One MCP server's config, in Codex's `[mcp_servers.<name>]` shape: a
`command` for a server Koda starts, or a `url` for one it reaches over
streamable HTTP.

bearer_token_env_var.description:
The environment variable that holds the bearer token. The token
itself is never stored.

command.description: The command that starts the server.

http_headers.description: Headers sent with every HTTP request.

omit_tools_from.description:
Where the server's tools are left out, as Codex's `omit_tools_from`:
`["deferred"]` sends them up front even to a model with tool search.

required.description:
A session doesn't start without it: `session/start` fails when it
fails to start.

startup_timeout_sec.description: Seconds the server has to start (default 30).

tool_input_schema_max_bytes.description:
The size, in bytes of compact JSON, past which a tool's input schema
is shrunk, as Codex's `tool_input_schema_max_bytes` (default 5,000).

url.description: The server's URL, for streamable HTTP.

McpServerConnectionStatus.description: Where a server's connection stands; Codex's values that Koda produces.

oneOf.description: Not started: stored, but no session has it.

McpServerElicitationAction.description: What the user did with an elicitation: MCP's actions.

oneOf.description: Said no; the tool goes on without it.

McpServerElicitationRequestParams.description:
`mcpServer/elicitation/request`: an MCP server asks the user for input
in the middle of a tool call, as MCP's `elicitation/create` and Codex's
request of the same name. Form mode asks for the fields in
`requestedSchema`; URL mode asks the user to visit `url`.

message.description: What the server says it needs.

requestedSchema.description:
Form mode: a JSON Schema object of flat, primitive fields (string,
number, integer, boolean, string enums).

url.description: URL mode: the page to visit.

content.description: The fields' values, for an accepted form.

McpServerOauthLoginParams.description:
`mcpServer/oauth/login`: sign in to a configured streamable HTTP server
with OAuth, as Codex's. The answer gives the page to open; the host waits
for the browser's redirect, stores the tokens and sends
`mcpServer/oauthLogin/completed`. Open sessions then reconnect to their
servers.

name.description: The server's name in the config.

authorizationUrl.description: The authorization server's page, to open in a browser.

McpServerOauthLogoutParams.description:
`mcpServer/oauth/logout`: forget a server's stored OAuth tokens. Koda's
own method; Codex forgets them in `codex mcp logout`.

removed.description: Whether there were tokens to forget.

McpServerRefreshParams.description:
`config/mcpServer/reload`: every open session takes the configured servers
again, starting new ones, stopping removed ones and restarting changed
or failed ones, before its next turn. Answered once the idle sessions
have taken them, so a `mcpServerStatus/list` that follows shows the
change; new servers are then still starting.

McpServerStatus.description: One server as a session has it.

authStatus.description:
How Koda authenticates to it, as Codex's `authStatus`. Given in the
configured listing (no `sessionId`).

resources.description:
The resources it offers, as Codex lists them: what `@server:uri`
names in a message. MCP Apps pages (`ui://`) are left out.

toolsError.description: Why it has no tools, when it failed.

McpServerStatusUpdatedNotification.description:
`mcpServer/startupStatus/updated`: a session's server started, failed
or was stopped while starting.

description.description: What it does, as the server says.

text.description: What they say; absent until something is saved there.

MemoryScope.description: Which of Koda's notes: the session's project's or everyone's.

Mention.description: A file or directory mentioned in a turn's input.

path.description: Its path, as the user wrote it.

MergeStrategy.description: How an edit's value merges with what's there.

oneOf.description: Merge into it; for a string, the same as replace.

anyOf.description: A call that expects a response.

Message.description:
Any message on the wire, in either direction.

The variants are told apart by their members, as the specification
does: a request has `id` and `method`, a notification `method` only, a
response `result`, an error `error`.

alias.description:
The alias this entry is, such as `claude-opus`, which follows its
line. A pick by alias should be made by it.

id.description:
The id to send, or `auto-detect` for `local`, whose model the server
names.

baseUrl.description: The provider's endpoint. Without one, its default.

modelProvider.description: The provider, by id. Without one, the host's.

data.description:
The models, aliases first. For Anthropic, the newest model of each
line, not every model it lists.

ModelProviderApiKeyRemoveParams.description:
`modelProvider/apiKey/remove`: forget a provider's stored key. One set
in the environment Koda was started with stays.

ModelProviderApiKeySetParams.description:
`modelProvider/apiKey/set`: store a provider's API key. Koda keeps a key
per provider, which Codex, whose `account/login/start` signs in one
OpenAI account, doesn't. The key never comes back in any response.

base_url.description:
The provider's endpoint, used whenever a session runs on it and
names none.

request_max_retries.description: Retries a failed request gets after the first try.

stream_idle_timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds a reply may go silent before the connection counts as
lost; 0 turns the limit off.

stream_max_retries.description: Retries for a reply whose stream failed partway.

data.description: The providers, in the order a picker shows them.

defaultProviderId.description: The host's provider, which a new session uses by default.

ModelProviderSummary.description: One provider. Codex's `ModelProviderSummary`, with Koda's key status.

envKey.description:
The environment variable its key comes from, such as
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, as Codex's `ModelProviderInfo.env_key`.

hasApiKey.description: Whether a key is set for it. Never the key itself.

name.description: The name a person reads, such as `LM Studio`.

requiresApiKey.description: Whether it needs an API key.

Notification.description: A one-way message: nothing answers it.

OverriddenMetadata.description: What wins over a write, as Codex reports it.

effectiveValue.description: The value in force, for the first overridden key.

overridingLayer.description: The layer whose value is in force.

PatchChangeKind.description: What happens to a file, as Codex's `PatchChangeKind` says.

oneOf.description: A file changed, and moved when `movePath` is set.

movePath.description: Where it moves to. Koda's tools never move a file.

PlanStepStatus.description: How far a plan step got.

Request.description: A call that expects a [`Response`] or an [`ErrorResponse`] with the same id.

anyOf.description: A numeric id. Koda's own clients use these.

RequestId.description: A request id, chosen by whoever sends the request.

Response.description: The result of a request that succeeded.

Retry.description: A model call that will be tried again.

attempt.description: The attempt that failed, counting from 1.

delayMs.description: The wait before the next one.

maxAttempts.description: The attempts the call gets in all.

RetryReason.description: Why a model call is tried again.

oneOf.description: The provider said to slow down.
A connection failed or timed out.
The provider answered with a server error.
The reply's stream failed partway; what it had shown is discarded.
The context was too long; it was compacted first.

SandboxConfigValue.description: `[sandbox]`: what sandboxed commands may do beyond Koda's defaults.

allow_local_binding.description:
macOS: let commands use any local port, not only the servers Koda
started.

available.description: Whether it works on this machine. Auto mode needs it.

setupHint.description:
What to do about it, when it doesn't: how to install or enable the
backend, or to use Safe mode. For a person, a few lines.

ServeStopParams.description:
`serve/stop`: stop the shared server, as `claude daemon stop` stops
Claude Code's supervisor. Only `koda serve` takes it; a host in the
client's process refuses it.

ifIdle.description:
Stop only if nothing would be lost: no open session and no other
client. A TUI that finds a server of another version asks this way.

ServeStopResponse.description: The answer to `serve/stop`, sent before the server stops.

reason.description: Why it isn't, when it isn't.

ServerRequestResolvedNotification.description:
`serverRequest/resolved`: a request needs no answer any more. Other
clients dismiss their prompt. In `koda exec`, Koda answers its own
requests and sends this right after each.

Session.description:
A session: one stored conversation. Codex's `Thread`. What it's running
with (`model` through `instruction_sources`) is there only while it is
open, as from `session/start`; `session/list` gives stored sessions
without it.

createdAt.description: When it was created, in Unix seconds.

cwd.description: The project it works in; absent for sessions too old to record it.

id.description: The session's id, for resuming it.

instructionSources.description:
The instruction files (`AGENTS.md` and the like) its prompt carries,
in that order: the global one, then the project's from the git root
down. Codex's `instructionSources`, as of the session's opening.

mode.description:
What Koda may do without asking: the mode an open session runs in,
and for a listed one the mode it last ran in, which resuming it
keeps.

name.description: Its title, set from the first prompt.

preview.description: The first user message; empty before there is one.

tools.description: The tools the model is offered.

turns.description:
Its turns, oldest first, each with its items. Filled only by
`session/start` resuming a session and by `session/read` with
`includeTurns`, as Codex's `Thread.turns` is.

Each turn is the one the client saw: its id, status, usage and
completed items, a sub-agent's tool calls under its `InvokeAgent`
call. A turn that never ended, Koda having stopped mid-way, reads as
interrupted.

Sessions from before Koda stored turns (0.6.4 and earlier) are
rebuilt from the messages the model read, which keep less: a turn's id
is its first message's, an interrupted turn followed by a new prompt
reads as one turn, a tool call's status is read from its output, its
`detail` and `changes` are missing, a sub-agent's tool calls and
compactions aren't listed, and turns have no usage or duration.

updatedAt.description: When its last message was stored, in Unix seconds.

SessionCompactStartParams.description:
`session/compact/start`: compact an open session's history now, as
Codex's `thread/compact/start`. Answered at once; the compaction runs as
a turn of its own (`turn/started`, a `contextCompaction` item with the
`manual` trigger, `turn/completed`). A running turn is stopped first and
ends interrupted. The compaction's turn can be interrupted, not steered.

SessionDeleteParams.description:
`session/delete`: delete a stored session. An open one is closed first,
its running turn stopped, as Codex's `thread/delete` does.

sessionId.description: The session, by its full id.

SessionForkParams.description:
`session/fork`: a new session with a copy of a stored one's history,
opened and ready for a turn, as Codex's `thread/fork` does. The copy
is named "Fork of" the source's name and keeps its provider, endpoint,
model and mode unless others are named, as `session/start` resumes a
session; the source is left as it was. Whatever the source has stored
is copied, so a turn still running there is copied as far as it has
got.

approvalPolicy.description: Who answers the fork's requests. Without one, the client does.

baseUrl.description: The provider's endpoint, as `session/start` takes it.

config.description: Config values for the copy only, as `session/start` takes them.

cwd.description:
The folder the copy works in, as `session/start` takes it; the copy
belongs to it.

model.description: The model: an id or an alias, as `session/start` takes it.

modelProvider.description: The provider, by id, as `session/start` takes it.

sessionId.description: The session to fork, by its full id.

SessionForkResponse.description:
The answer to `session/fork`: the fork, opened, with its turns, as
`session/start` returns a resumed session.

session.description: The fork, ready for a turn.

SessionGoalClearParams.description:
`session/goal/clear`: remove an open session's goal. A turn on it that
is running goes on to its end; no other starts. `session/goal/cleared`
follows when there was one.

cleared.description: Whether the session had a goal.

goal.description: The goal, if the session has one.

SessionGoalHeldNotification.description:
`session/goal/judged`: with `goal_judge = "evaluator"` (Claude Code's
`session/goal/held`: Koda stopped starting turns on the goal, which
stays set, after goal turns in a row that called no tool, as Claude
Code stops a goal loop that answers without working. The user's next
message, or `/goal resume`, goes on with it. Koda's own.

turnId.description: The turn after which it stopped.

turns.description: How many goal turns in a row called no tool.

SessionGoalJudgedNotification.description:
way), the check after a turn on an active goal found it met, not yet
met, or impossible.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence or two, if it said.

SessionGoalSetParams.description:
`session/goal/set`: set an open session's goal, or change it.

With an `objective` and no goal, a new goal starts, active unless
`status` says otherwise. With a goal, the fields given change it: a new
objective is told to the model at its next step. Without an objective,
the session must have a goal. Setting an active goal on an idle session
starts a turn on it. `session/goal/updated` follows.

objective.description: The objective: not empty, at most 4,000 characters.

tokenBudget.description:
The token budget: a positive number, or `null` for none. Absent
keeps it.

SessionGoalUpdatedNotification.description:
`session/goal/updated`: a session's goal was set or changed, by a client,
by the model, or by Koda as it counted a turn's use or stopped the goal.

turnId.description: The turn that changed it, if one did.

cursor.description:
Where to go on from: an earlier answer's `nextCursor`, as Codex's
`thread/list` pages. Without one, the most recent.

cwd.description: The project whose sessions to list; without one, the host's.

limit.description: How many at most; without one, 50.

data.description: The sessions, without what open ones are running with.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque; pass it as `cursor` for the next page. Absent when there are
no more, as Codex's `nextCursor`.

SessionMemoryAddParams.description:
`session/memory/add`: save `text` to the notes. Text that starts with a
`## Heading` replaces the section with that heading, if there is one,
as `MemoryWrite` does. The session's next turn reads it.

SessionMemoryReadResponse.description:
The answer to `session/memory/read`: the project's notes, then the
global ones, each as the model reads it.

notes.description: The project's notes, then the global ones.

SessionNameSetParams.description:
`session/name/set`: name a stored session, as Codex's `thread/name/set`
does. The name replaces the title Koda takes from the first prompt, and
a later prompt doesn't replace it. `session/name/updated` follows.

name.description: The new name: not empty, at most 100 characters.

sessionId.description: The session, by its full id.

SessionReadParams.description:
`session/read`: a stored session, without opening it. Codex's
`thread/read`.

includeTurns.description: Whether to return its turns and their items.

sessionId.description: The session, by its full id.

session.description: The session as `session/list` gives it, with its turns when asked.

SessionRewindParams.description:
`session/rewind`: take a turn and every turn after it out of an open,
idle session's history, as Codex's `thread/revert` replaces a thread's
history with the part before one turn. Files the turns changed stay as
they are. Refused while a turn runs, for a turn from before Koda
recorded where turns start (0.7.8), and across a compaction.

beforeTurnId.description: The first turn taken out, as `session/turns/list` names it.

SessionSettings.description: What a session's turns run with.

alias.description: The alias the model was chosen by, if any.

effort.description: The reasoning effort sent, if any.

SessionSettingsUpdateParams.description:
`session/settings/update`: what the session's next turns run with, as
Codex's `thread/settings/update`. Only what's given changes. A running
turn keeps its own; `session/settings/updated` follows once applied.
The provider can't change: a model of another provider is refused.

model.description: The model: an id, or an alias of the session's provider.

settings.description: All of its settings, as they are now.

approvalPolicy.description: Who answers the session's requests. Without one, the client does.

baseUrl.description:
The provider's endpoint, for a local server or a gateway. Without
one, the provider's default, or a resumed session's own. Given
without `modelProvider` for a new session, it names the provider
too, by its host or local port, as `koda --base-url` does.

config.description:
Config values for this session only, over the config file and the
host's own, as `-c key=value` gives them and as Codex's
`thread/start` takes a `config` map: dotted keys, JSON values.

cwd.description:
The folder the session works in, as Codex's `thread/start` takes a
`cwd`: an absolute path to an existing folder. Without one, the
host's. One shared server serves every project this way.

model.description:
The model: an id, or an alias such as `claude-opus`, which follows
its line's newest model. Without one, the provider's default, or a
resumed session's own choice, an alias resolved again.

modelProvider.description:
The provider, by id (`anthropic`, `lm-studio`, …, as
`modelProvider/list` gives them). A new session without one uses the
host's; a resumed one keeps the provider it was started with, as
Codex's `thread/resume` does. A session's provider never changes.

sessionId.description:
An earlier session to resume, by its full id, as Codex's
`thread/resume` takes one; a client matches a shorter one over
`session/list`. Without one, a new session starts.

session.description: The session, ready for a turn.

SessionStartedNotification.description: `session/started`: a session is ready for its first turn.

protocolVersion.description: [`crate::PROTOCOL_VERSION`]. A reader that can't read it should stop.

SessionTokenUsageUpdatedNotification.description:
`session/tokenUsage/updated`: what an open session's model calls have
used, and how full its context is. Codex's `thread/tokenUsage/updated`,
sent before each model call and when a turn's last call is done.

SessionTurnsListParams.description:
`session/turns/list`: a page of a session's turns, with their items, as
Codex's `thread/turns/list` pages a thread's. A client that loads only a
session's recent turns (a phone, a long session) fetches older ones as it
needs them.

cursor.description:
Where to go on from: an earlier answer's `nextCursor`, or its
`backwardsCursor` with the other `sortDirection`. Without one, the
newest turns (or the oldest, ascending).

limit.description: How many turns at most: 25 without one, at most 100.

sessionId.description: The session, by its full id; open or not.

sortDirection.description: Newest first (`desc`, without one) or oldest first (`asc`).

backwardsCursor.description:
Opaque; pass it as `cursor` with the other `sortDirection` to read
back from this page's first turn, that turn included, to catch what
changed in it (a turn that was running). Absent on an empty page.

data.description:
The turns, in the order asked for, each with its items. A turn still
running is `inProgress`, with the items it has so far.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque; pass it as `cursor` for the next page in the same order.
Absent when there are no more.

SessionUnsubscribeParams.description:
`session/unsubscribe`: the client is done with a session. Its running
turn, if any, stops, and the session is closed; `session/start` with its
id opens it again. Codex's `thread/unsubscribe`.

SessionUnsubscribeStatus.description:
What `session/unsubscribe` did. Codex also has `notSubscribed`, for a
session other clients still hold; a Koda host has one client.

oneOf.description: The session was open, and now isn't.
No session with that id was open.

SkillErrorInfo.description: A skill file that couldn't be loaded.

SkillInput.description: A skill the user picked, by its name as `skills/list` gives it.

path.description: Its `SKILL.md`, as `skills/list` gives it; the name decides.

description.description: What it's for, in one line.

enabled.description:
Whether the model may use it. Always true: Koda can't disable a
skill yet.

path.description: Its `SKILL.md`. Optional in Koda: a built-in skill has no file.

userInvocable.description:
Whether a person picks it, as opposed to only the model
(`user_invocable: false` in its frontmatter). Koda's own; Codex has
none.

SkillScope.description:
Where a skill comes from, in Codex's names. A project's overrides a
user's, which overrides a built-in one of the same name. Codex also has
`admin`, for skills an administrator installs.

errors.description: The skill files found there that couldn't be loaded.

SkillsListParams.description:
`skills/list`. Codex's also takes `forceReload`; Koda finds the model's
skills once, when its agent is built, so a reload would list skills the
model can't use.

cwds.description: The folders to list skills for; without any, the host's project.

SkillsListResponse.description: The answer to `skills/list`: one entry per folder asked about.

data.description: The entries, in the order asked.

SortDirection.description: The order a page runs in. Codex's `SortDirection`.

StateReadResponse.description:
The model, provider, context window, mode and sandbox a new session
starts with.

mode.description: What Koda may do without asking.

byAgent.description:
`total` by agent, with its model calls: the session's own under
`main`, each sub-agent's under its name. Koda's own: a Codex
sub-agent is a thread with its own usage, while Koda's run inside
the session's turn, so the split is sent here.

last.description: The latest model call of the session's own: not a sub-agent's.

total.description:
Every model call since the session was created: its turns,
sub-agents and compactions. A resumed session's count starts from
what its stored calls used, as Codex restores a thread's.

TokenUsageBreakdown.description: Tokens of one model call, or added up. Codex's `TokenUsageBreakdown`.

cacheWriteInputTokens.description: Input tokens written to the provider's cache.

cachedInputTokens.description: Input tokens read from the provider's cache.

ToolCallApprovalParams.description: `item/toolCall/requestApproval`: a tool call needs a yes before it runs.

allowForSession.description:
Whether `approveForSession` may be answered: only for local changes
inside the project.

changes.description: The file changes it would make, as on its item.

detail.description: What the call would do, in a line.

ToolCallOutputDeltaNotification.description: `item/toolCall/outputDelta`: a line of a running command's output.

delta.description: The output, ending in a newline.

ToolCallProgressNotification.description:
`item/toolCall/progress`: a notice about a running tool call, such as a
sub-agent reaching its turn limit. Codex's `item/mcpToolCall/progress`,
for Koda's one tool-call item.

oneOf.description: It ran and did what was asked.

It ran and failed: bad arguments, an error, a timeout, or a command
that exited non-zero.

It never ran: refused at an approval, by plan mode or by a
sub-agent's limits.
The turn stopped before or while it ran.

ToolEffect.description: What a tool call does, and so whether it needs a yes.

oneOf.description:
Read only: reads, searches and read-only commands run; anything else
is refused. For sub-agents and `koda exec` runs that should only
look.
Every action with a side effect asks first.

Mutating actions run without asking, contained by the sandbox;
destructive actions and writes outside the project still ask.

TuiConfigValue.description: `[tui]`: settings a TUI reads from its own machine's file.

syntax_highlight.description: Colour code blocks and diffs; `false` for plain text.

Turn.description: A turn. `turn/started` sends it in progress, `turn/completed` finished.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time, set when the turn is over.

error.description:
Why it failed, when it did; and on an interrupted turn, why it
didn't stop cleanly, when it was dropped where it stood.

items.description:
Its items, in order. Filled only when a stored session's turns are
returned, by `session/start` resuming it, `session/read` or
`session/turns/list`, as Codex's `Turn.items` is; empty on `turn/started` and
`turn/completed`, whose items come as notifications.

usage.description:
What it used: tokens and model calls, sub-agents and compaction
included. Set when the turn is over.

TurnCompletedNotification.description:
`turn/completed`: the turn is over, however it ended. Exactly one per
turn.

code.description:
What kind of failure, for a client to act on, when Koda knows one,
as Codex's turn errors carry `codexErrorInfo`.

TurnErrorCode.description: What kind of failure a [`TurnError`] is.

oneOf.description:
The turn spent its token budget (`turn_token_budget`) and stopped
before its next model call. What it did so far stays in the session.

turnId.description: The turn to stop. Refused when it isn't the one running.

TurnInterruptResponse.description: The answer to `turn/interrupt`, sent once the turn has stopped.

TurnItem.description:
An item of a stored turn, as `session/start` (resuming) and
`session/read` return it: what `item/completed` sent, with its parent
and its times, as Codex's `ThreadItem` keeps them.

completedAtMs.description: When it completed, in Unix milliseconds; absent when not recorded.

parentItemId.description: On a sub-agent's items: the tool call that started the sub-agent.

startedAtMs.description:
When it started, in Unix milliseconds; absent when not recorded, as
in sessions stored before Koda recorded it.

TurnLoopGuardNotification.description:
`turn/loopGuard`: the model kept repeating itself. Koda's own; Codex has
none.

TurnPlanUpdatedNotification.description: `turn/plan/updated`: the model rewrote its plan (its todo list).

clientMessageId.description: The client's id for the message, echoed on its `userMessage` item.

mentions.description:
Files and directories the user mentioned (`@path`), which the host
reads and sends the model with the text, as Claude Code includes an
`@` file. A path is relative to the session's project, or absolute,
on the host's machine.

mode.description:
The trust mode from this turn on. Without one, the session keeps
its own.

outputSchema.description:
A JSON Schema the last reply of this turn, and of the turns Koda
starts after it on its own (a goal's, a background command's), must
match, as Codex's `outputSchema`. The prompt says so; a reply that
doesn't match gets one more model call with the schema enforced by
the API. A `turn/start` without one clears it.

skills.description:
Skills the user picked, as Codex's `UserInput::Skill`: the host sends
the model each one's instructions with the text. A `$name` in `input`
that names a skill counts too, so a client that keeps `$name` in the
text needn't send these.

oneOf.description: The user or client stopped it.

clientMessageId.description:
The client's id for the text, echoed on the `userMessage` item that
delivers it.

expectedTurnId.description: The turn the text is for. Refused when it isn't the one running.

TurnSteerResponse.description: The answer to `turn/steer`: the text is queued for the turn.

turnId.description: The turn it was queued for.

cacheCreationTokens.description: Input tokens written to the provider's cache.

cachedInputTokens.description: Input tokens read from the provider's cache.

UserInputParams.description: `item/tool/requestUserInput`: the model asked the user a question.

options.description: Answer choices; empty for a free answer.

sessionId.description: The session, when it concerns one.

oneOf.description:
Saved, but a `-c` value for this run wins over it until Koda
restarts.
